title: M3: cross-reference deps x refs for module-split planning
description: Answer: 'if package X lives in module A and Y in module B, which symbols cross the boundary?' Neither `deps` (package-level) nor `refs` (symbol-level) answers directly. New query combining package sets with symbol-level cross-boundary refs. Hard: query surface design, output shape, perf on large graphs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Design doc approved before impl (requires_plan)
- New query accepts two package sets (glob or list) and returns symbols whose refs cross the boundary
- Output shape: symbol, kind, source pkg, target pkg, ref location
- Performance: <500ms on snipe's own graph
- Blackbox test on a fixture with a known cross-boundary ref
- Reviewed before merge

title: M1: string literal / env var tracking
description: New index surface for tracking string constants and env var names (e.g. SNIPE_VOYAGE_API_KEY used in 9 places via os.Getenv). Neither `def` nor `refs` finds them today because they are literals, not Go symbols. Hard: new extraction pipeline, storage schema impact, query surface design.
acceptance_criteria:
- Design doc approved before impl (requires_plan)
- Index extracts string-literal constants and os.Getenv arg names
- Query surface (name TBD in design) returns file:line refs for a given literal
- Schema migration is forward-only and safe on existing .snipe DBs
- Blackbox test: SNIPE_VOYAGE_API_KEY resolves to all 9 known call sites
- Indexing overhead <10% on snipe's own repo
- make ci green; reviewed before merge

title: M4: snipe pack for packages (not just symbols)
description: Extend `snipe pack` to accept a package path (e.g. `snipe pack internal/mcp`). Output: exports, imports, dependency count, test count, LOC, key types. Reuse existing pack plumbing where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- snipe pack accepts a package path (e.g. internal/mcp) in addition to symbol names
- Output includes: exports, imports, dependency count, test count, LOC, key types
- Clean error on non-existent package path (not a crash)
- Blackbox fixture test covers a known package end-to-end
- Symbol-path behavior unchanged (regression guard)
- make ci green

title: M5: fold internal deps DAG into context --boot output
description: Per boot.md: 'Cheap M5 first: fold deps internal DAG into context --boot output'. Compact package-dependency section added to `snipe context --boot` so Claude gets the DAG at session start without extra `snipe deps` calls. Keep token budget tight.
acceptance_criteria:
- snipe context --boot emits a compact internal package DAG section
- Section adds <500 output tokens on snipe's own repo
- Blackbox test: DAG section present when packages exist, omitted when zero-value
- Existing context --boot fields unchanged
- make ci green

title: Finish v0.1.0 audit remainder (M1/M3/M4/M5)
description: GH #126 — remainder after wave A/B/C (F1-F10, M2, M6 already shipped as of commit 091b097). Four independent improvements surfaced by the trixi audit: M5 (deps DAG in boot context), M4 (pack for packages), M1 (string/env var tracking), M3 (deps×refs cross-ref for module split planning).

- M1, M3, M4, M5 subtasks all merged to main
- boot.md updated to reflect remaining-audit completion
- GH #126 closed with commit references

title: lifecycle: blackbox fixture test + docs

title: lifecycle: text + JSON output formatters
description: Render grouped CRUD sections with caller chains (arrow notation `a ← b ← c`) as claudish text default; JSON variant with structured groups for orca. Respect --max-tokens.
acceptance_criteria:

title: lifecycle: caller-chain assembly per CRUD group
description: For each CRUD-classified function, walk callers (existing ref graph) to build entry-point chains. Reuse internal/query caller traversal. Bound depth to avoid explosion on hot symbols.
acceptance_criteria:
- For each classified fn, walks callers up to bounded depth (default 3, configurable via flag)
- Output: entry-point chains per fn
- Cycle detection prevents infinite recursion on mutual recursion
- Reuses internal/query caller traversal — no duplicated graph walk
- Unit test on a fixture with known chains of depth 1, 2, and 3
- make ci green

title: lifecycle: scaffold subcommand (flags, cobra wiring, knownSubcommands)
description: Add `cmd/lifecycle.go` with cobra wiring, flags (Type positional, --format, --max-tokens). Register in knownSubcommands in cmd/root.go. No business logic yet — return stub. Verified by `snipe lifecycle Foo` invoking without crash and `make check` green.
acceptance_criteria:
- cmd/lifecycle.go exists with cobra wiring
- Flags: positional Type, --format, --max-tokens
- Registered in knownSubcommands in cmd/root.go
- snipe lifecycle Foo exits 0 with a stub payload — no crash, no business logic yet
- make check green

title: lifecycle: CRUD classification heuristics (Create/Mutate/Read/Delete)
description: Classify each function referencing the target type. Heuristics: Create = returns *Type or assigns Type{}; Mutate = takes *Type and writes fields; Read = takes Type/*Type without mutation; Delete = Delete/Remove/Archive naming or nils the ref. Unit-tested on fixture types with known CRUD shapes. Hard: signature analysis + mutation detection via go/ast — unknowns in accuracy tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Design doc approved before impl (requires_plan)
- Classifier assigns one of {Create, Mutate, Read, Delete} per function referencing the target type
- Unit tests cover: constructor returning *T, struct literal T{}, pointer-receiver mutation, read-only access, Delete/Remove/Archive naming
- Ambiguous fns surfaced explicitly (not silently dropped)
- Runs on snipe's own repo without panics
- Reviewed before merge; make ci green

title: Ship snipe lifecycle — type mutation graph command
description: GH #135. New command `snipe lifecycle <Type>` that traces every function creating, mutating, reading, or deleting instances of a type, grouped by CRUD, with caller chains. Replaces the manual 5+ query stitching that the `lifecycle-trace` skill currently guides. See GH #135 for full proposal and output examples.
acceptance_criteria:
- snipe lifecycle <Type> shipped and documented in .claude/rules/CLAUDE.md
- All 5 subtasks (scaffold, heuristics, chains, formatters, fixture) merged
- lifecycle-trace skill updated to invoke the new command instead of stitching 5+ queries
- GH #135 closed with commit references
- make ci green

value: When finishing an epic in beads, close any related/child issues that are done in the same pass — don't leave orphan children open under a closed epic. Also check for sibling issues or GH issues referenced in labels/description that may have been resolved by the epic's work.

When finishing an epic in beads, also close any related GitHub issues referenced in the epic (gh_issue metadata, gh-NNN labels, or GH #NNN in description). Use 'gh issue close NNN -c "resolved by <commit/PR>"' and cross-link. Don't leave GH issues open after the work has shipped.
